section.title: Purpose
section.para: This document states the system requirements (SRQs) of JetOS. The high level requirements of the JetOS functions, which are written in the headers of the functions and published in the function documentation (docs/kernel.pdf, docs/boards.pdf and docs/shared.pdf), are traced to the requirements of this document.

section.title: Scope: what JetOS is
section.para: In this document, JetOS is the software that runs in the privileged mode of the processor of a module and shares the module between partitions. It consists of:

listitem.para: the kernel (kernel/): the architecture independent core (kernel/core), the debugging support (kernel/debug), the CPU support packages of the supported processor architectures, x86_64 and arm64 (kernel/csps), and the board support packages, x86_64-qemu and arm64-qemu (kernel/bsps);
the library and the headers that the kernel shares with the hypervisor (common/ and include/), as they are used by the kernel.

section.para: The following are not part of JetOS as defined here, and have, or will have, requirements documents of their own:

listitem.para: the examples, the tests and the benchmarks.

section.para: The services that the kernel provides to partitions through system calls, including those that the APEX interface is built on (partitions, processes, time, ports, health monitoring), are in the scope of this document; they are stated as the behaviour of the kernel, not as the APEX services.

section.title: Conventions
section.para: A requirement has an identifier of the form SRQ_JET_AREA_NNN, where AREA names the chapter of the requirement. An identifier is never changed and never used again for another requirement. A requirement states one behaviour of JetOS that can be verified, with exactly one shall (a requirement with two is split into two requirements); its rationale, its verification method (test, analysis or review) and its traceability follow it. The traceability lists the high level requirements of the functions that trace to the requirement, or says Not applicable for a constraint on the whole software, which no single function implements.

listitem.para: The computer that JetOS runs on: a processor, its memory and its devices.
A program that JetOS runs in the unprivileged mode of the processor, in an address space and in time windows of its own.
The time since the start of the module, in nanoseconds.
The unit of execution inside a partition, as in ARINC 653 (a thread in the code).
A slot is an interval of the schedule of the module, given to one partition or to a service of the kernel; a major frame is the sequence of all the slots, which the module repeats for ever.
A port is the end of a channel in a partition, through which the partition sends or receives messages; a channel connects a source port with a destination port.
The detection of errors of the module and of the partitions, and the recovery from them by the actions of configured tables.
A mutual exclusion region of a partition, managed in the memory of the partition with the help of the kernel.
